text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS @

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn said that the Democratic Forum and other parties are making desperate efforts to bring down the cabinet. Erno Kiss, head of the Central Crime Fighting Directorate, told the session of a parliamentary investigative commission that one confession and evidence backed up by official documents bear out the charge that Socialist Party treasurer Laszlo Boldvai, and Gyorgy Budai, an entrepreneur with links to the Free Democrats, requested a share of the fee paid to lawyer Marta Tocsik. Socialist Party executive vice-president Magda Kovacs Kosa described the Forum's no-confidence proposal as a stage in the election campaign. @
- Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski wound up two days of official talks in Budapest Tuesday with a proposal to breathe new life into Visegrad co-operation.

- The state programme of transferring assets to social security organisations for free closed yesterday with an agreement between social security authorities and the State Privatisation and Holding Co.
- The US, Autralia, Argentina and New Zealand file in a complaint about Hungary's excess agricultural subsidies to the World Trade Organisation today, the Australian trade minister announced. @

- A portfolio of HUF 300 billion in minority shares held by the state will be transferred from the State Privatisation and Holding Co. to the Hungarian Development Bank, said Privatisation Minister Judit Csiha.
- Trading in compensation coupons was suspended yesterday after their market price dropped 30 percent.
- Piroska Apro was named board chairperson of the exhibition organiser Hungexpo at the general meeting following the dismissal of the old board of directors.
- A new state-owned bank will probably be established in the second half year to provide mortgage loans. @
- Police have caught two car theft rings responsible for HUF 1.2 billion in thefts in Budapest.

- Sandor Puhl was honoured as the Referee of the Year for the third time in a row by the German organisation IFFHS in Munich. Hungary's legendary striker Ferenc Puskas was named Goalscorer of the Century with 511 goals.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- Foreign Ministry spokesman Gabor Szentivanyi said "Hungary has never called into doubt Russia's right to stand up for its security interests, but it is convinced that NATO enlargement does not pose a threat to anyone". @
- The German government has instructed its Finance Ministry to work out details of support to be allocated to the Hungarian victims of the Holocaust.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- Smallholder president Jozsef Torgyan has notified Democratic Forum president Sandor Lezsak that he does not intend to hold consultations with the latter party on opposition cooperation in the future.
- The country's largest aluminum factory at Ajka may come to a standstill due to the cost increase in energy prices.
MAGYAR NEMZET @
- The Constitutional Court ruled Tuesday that the constitutional nature of international treaties concluded by Hungary could be subject to review in the future.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- AB-Aegon, Hungary's second largest insurance company, will be restructured into four business units, thus assuming a holding-like form, said managing director Gabor Kepecs.
